_comment.run: WAKE_DATA=/path/to/wake-data python -m near_wake.train --config recipes/train.json --stage all [--name RUN]. Paths are relative to $WAKE_DATA; outputs go to $WAKE_DATA/runs/<name>/ (hey_near.onnx, run.json, train.log).
_comment.name: Default run name; --name overrides it, e.g. to keep a run with and without the mishearings.
_comment.clips: Every synth run (en, vi, vi-slow) of each split, from synth/<split>/<run>/manifest.csv.
_comment.max_clips: Per split, a seeded sample of at most this many synthetic clips (for smoke runs); {} uses them all.
_comment.max_clip_seconds: Drops TTS glitches (a few clips came out 30-250 s long); real phrases and near-miss sentences are under 3.3 s.
_comment.exclude_negative_texts: [] trains on every near-miss. "mishearings" drops the negatives holding what the Vietnamese recognizer heard when users said Hey Near (texts.MISHEARINGS_VI): their sound may be exactly how users say it, so compare recall against false alarms with and without them.
_comment.exclude_negative_match: phrase: drop a clip whose text contains the phrase as whole words ("thầy này dạy hay lắm" holds "thầy này"); exact: only clips that say just the phrase.
_comment.real_dir: Real takes from near_wake.record ($WAKE_DATA/real/manifest.csv); used when there are any.
_comment.real_test_speakers: Held-out speakers for positive_test. null: one speaker in five (at least one once there are two), picked by a hash of the name.
_comment.real_repeat: Each real train take is augmented 20 times (each time with other noise and room), so a few hundred real takes weigh about as much as the ~19k synthetic positives they correct.
_comment.augmentation_rounds: One augmented copy per clip: there are already ~19k positives and ~14k near-misses from 6 voices with varied speed; raise it if the model overfits.
_comment.augmentation_batch_size: augment_clips gives a whole batch the same background clip and room: 16 (openwakeword's example) keeps that varied.
_comment.rir_dirs: Room impulse responses (MIT survey + SLR28 simulated rooms) for reverb, applied with probability 0.5.
_comment.background_dirs: Music and noise mixed in at -10..15 dB SNR with probability 0.75.
_comment.vi_speech_dir: 21 h of Vietnamese speech (no wake word), embedded once by --stage vi-negatives.
_comment.vi_speech_features: The shared cache of vi_speech_dir, (windows, 16, 96) float16 like ACAV100M.
_comment.negative_features: Big negatives: ACAV100M (2000 h of mostly non-Vietnamese audio, openwakeword's standard) and our Vietnamese speech, the language spoken around the device.
_comment.false_positive_validation: openwakeword's 10.7 h validation stream: false positives per hour during training, used to pick and merge checkpoints.
_comment.n_per_class: Rows per batch. ACAV100M 1024, positive 50 and adversarial_negative 50 are openwakeword's example values; vi_speech 512 makes Vietnamese a third of the general speech the model sees.
_comment.model_type: dnn: openwakeword's default fully connected model, cheap to run on the board every 80 ms.
_comment.layer_size: 32 units: openwakeword's example value; small enough not to memorize the TTS voices.
_comment.steps: 50000 (openwakeword's example) + 2 x 5000 fine-tuning steps: about 3 min on 4 CPU threads (2.7 s per 1000 steps measured, validations included). Features for the ~36k clips take about 7 min (~90 clips/s).
_comment.max_negative_weight: Negative loss weight ramps from 1 to this over the steps (openwakeword's example value). openwakeword 0.6.0 doubles it for each of the 2 later sequences regardless of the result, so it ends at 6000.
_comment.target_fp_per_hour: openwakeword's example value: 0.2 false activations per hour on the validation stream.
_comment.threads: CPU threads for augmentation, features (ThreadPool) and torch. 4 leaves the other cores free; training runs on the CPU (MPS is slower for this model).
_comment.seed: Seeds clip order, sampling and augmentation, so a run can be redone.
